acceptanceQuestion: Based only on the rendered public homepage, would this fictionalized Deborah Treisman editorial lens accept the page for publication?
nonEndorsementBoundary: Deborah Treisman is used only as a fictionalized analytical lens derived from public work; this evaluation is not her participation, quotation, endorsement, approval, or actual sign-off.
critique: The page earns publication under this criterion. “I help emerging work become usable systems” is a concise, memorable central sentence, and the supporting language immediately defines what “usable” means without smothering the proposition. The sequence is coherent: the opening photograph supplies human presence; the routing section respects a hurried hiring reader; proof points establish scale; six projects demonstrate the practice across materially different settings; capabilities abstract the transferable value; the five-verb method gives it rhythm; and the closing invitation names plausible next conversations. Photographs function as contextual evidence rather than decoration, with unusually responsible captions and collective-credit language. On mobile, however, the six-project run becomes very long, while repeated metadata, provenance qualifications, captions, and case-study links make the editorial spine less forceful than it is on desktop. The page occasionally approaches accumulated inventory, but the repeated idea of making work usable is developed through evidence, method, and handoff rather than merely restated.
strengths: The opening proposition is distinctive, plainspoken, and reinforced by concrete verbs: clarify, build, carry, and document.
The “Choose what you need to see” section gives time-constrained readers three intelligible routes without requiring them to decode the portfolio first.
Proof points introduce tenure, commercial effect, and documentation scale before the longer case studies ask for attention.
The projects span advocacy, civic data, commerce, resident service, publishing, and artist support while consistently identifying Jamie’s responsibility and what became usable.
Image captions add provenance, collective credit, and temporal context, strengthening trust rather than merely describing pictures.
“Listen. Map. Build. Document. Transfer.” is an effective late-page synthesis, and the invitation converts the narrative into a clear next step.
constructiveCriticism: The highest-value revision is to compress each mobile project’s metadata, qualification labels, and image caption into one short context line, leaving the role, outcome, and case-study link as the dominant reading path.

The “Capabilities” section partially repeats language already demonstrated in the projects; trimming each description to its most differentiating phrase would preserve the useful synthesis while improving momentum.

Rewrite the second proof point more directly—for example, foreground the specific intervention and then the 2x outcome—because “improvements contributed to” is less vivid and accountable than the surrounding evidence.
